analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md (no code, no config). I examined both head_text units (lines 4070-4923) against the patch hunks. The relevant changes: a bump of the last-updated date; text stating that a serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipeline defaults to 4 lanes (`DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes`); a new 'Gemma pipeline lanes' section (lines ~4506-4525); and an expanded expert-reduction paragraph (lines ~4901-4917) saying all tokens of a frame share one `SwitchGLU.callAndWeightedReduceRows` call with unsorted M=1 gathers.

Security-relevant claims I checked:
- Both owners derive the lane width from the same saved setup and bind it into the load agreement (`Gemma4BatchArithmeticAgreement`), so a mismatch fails closed. This is consistent with the documented fail-closed agreement pattern.
- Admission stays per-lane against live memory, and the activation floor is unchanged (relevant to the availability threats T-010/T-029).
- Cancellation is stated as 'retires alone' (`lanesRetireAlone`).
- The doc explicitly says the width is not hardware-qualified and that no serving grant follows. It does not claim confidentiality or attestation changes, so it does not overclaim runtime secrecy (T-056).
- The qualification-record section (lines 4540-4551) states that one alias gives no grant to the other.

A higher default lane count increases concurrent tenants and plaintext prompts resident in one process, plus the cross-request memory footprint. It does not change the trust boundaries TB-007/TB-003 or the prefix-cache posture (T-041). The doc says prefix reuse stays on the original chunk grid. The actual default and agreement binding live in code that is not supplied here (DistributedInstalledPlan, Gemma4BatchArithmeticAgreement). I cannot verify that the code matches the doc, or that the lane-memory admission is enforced. A reviewer of the code PR should confirm the width binding, the live-memory admission and the per-lane cancellation isolation. No security regression is evidenced in these doc units, and the threat model needs no update from documentation alone.
